issues: The summary says the Lord's work is completed before the king is punished, but verse 12 only says this will happen when the Lord has performed his work; the timing is not necessarily completed.
The visual inference of a diminished forest and field is permitted as prophetic imagery, but the passage does not establish that this is a literal visible event.
The summary's 'tracks' and reasonable inference of movement could imply one staged continuous journey; preserve the successive locations and avoid collapsing them into one scene.
'The passage calls to the daughter of Gallim' may imply an identifiable speaker; the verse does not identify who says the words.
The visual inference that trees are being cut down risks treating the bough and forest imagery as literal; the text does not specify whether these are literal or figurative.
